Instrument services, define the signals that matter, and make security data reliable and useful. - Engineer investigations and threat hunting: Build tools and workflows for proactive hunting, evidence collection, incident scoping, and containment. Turn investigation findings into new detections and lasting improvements. - Use agents to scale the team: Build reliable internal AI agents and automation that triage alerts, enrich findings, gather evidence, scope incidents, and accelerate routine security work. Design human-in-the-loop controls and evaluations so automation is safe, observable, and trustworthy. - Lead incident response and participate in on-call: Triage, scope, contain, and remediate security incidents, then drive postmortems that produce durable engineering changes. - Partner with Product Security: Turn product threat models and vulnerability findings into production monitoring, and feed real-world detection and incident learnings back into secure design. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - 5+ years in security engineering, with meaningful experience in detection engineering, security operations, or incident response — and the software skills to build your way out of repetitive work. - Strong software engineering in Python or Go (TypeScript a plus). WHAT YOU'LL OWN: Carry multi-quarter programs - Own the Salesforce sales process from lead to close — routing, qualification, territory assignment, and stage progression — driving each initiative from discovery through UAT, change management, and adoption. - Be the person stakeholders come to before they file a request, especially when the system was never designed for what the business now needs. - Own the intake and prioritization model for hundreds of quarterly GTM systems requests, ensuring the team works on the highest-leverage business problems rather than the loudest tickets. Own what gets specified and what ships - Run discovery and turn ambiguous asks into BRDs, process flows, data models, and acceptance criteria — with a clear problem statement and ROI justification, precise enough to execute without a second conversation. - Hold the quality gate: you write the specification, engineers and coding agents write the code, and nothing reaches production without your sign-off. - Run vendor evaluations when the right answer is buy, integrate, or replace rather than build. Protect revenue data integrity - Trace anomalies in revenue fields — Net ARR, initial pipeline, lead source — back to the automation, trigger, or integration that wrote them. - Own the reconciliation seam between Salesforce, usage-based billing, and cloud-marketplace transactions. - Identify which design decisions are load-bearing and which are cosmetic, and catch the downstream failure modes before they reach production. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE: In your first 6–12 months, you might: - Redesign the lead-to-opportunity process so routing, qualification, and stage progression are measurable, enforceable, and adopted by the field. - Create a prioritization model for hundreds of GTM systems requests per quarter, with clear tradeoffs and business rationale. - Ship a Salesforce change that improves pipeline hygiene, quote-to-cash accuracy, provisioning reliability, or cloud marketplace reconciliation. - Establish a specification and UAT standard that engineers and AI agents can reliably build against. - Build enough trust with Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance that stakeholders bring you the problem before they prescribe the solution. WHAT YOU'LL NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL: SYSTEMS AND DOMAIN DEPTH - Domain and tenure — 6–8 years in business systems, sales systems, revenue systems, or GTM systems, with Salesforce as your primary platform throughout. - Sales process depth — you've partnered with Sales Ops on the things reps feel every day: territory and account coverage, lead qualification and routing, stage gates, and pipeline and forecast hygiene. - Sales systems / RevOps depth — experience across quote-to-cash, CPQ, territory and lead routing, forecasting, or adjacent revenue processes. - Technical fluency — you can read a data model, a Flow, and enough Apex to design against what's really there, even though you are not expected to write production code. PROGRAM LEADERSHIP - Program ownership — you've been the single accountable owner, at the working level negotiating the commitments yourself, of a program that spanned four or more functions and changed how a revenue org works day to day. - Release risk — you've delivered a program into a core system on a release process you didn't control, where another team's change could break your release. - Re-scoping under change — you've re-scoped a program mid-flight because the business changed under it, a sponsor moved, or the original scope no longer matched reality. - Holding the line — you've turned down a request with executive backing and kept the relationship; you hold the line when something breaks pricing discipline, a legal constraint, or the architecture, and you arrive with the alternative. JUDGMENT AND COMMUNICATION - One tradeoff, two audiences — you write for the reader in front of you, not the one you find easiest: the VP gets the page, the engineer gets the spec. - Maximum agency — you find the friction and start the project. You don't wait for a ticket. - AI judgment — you give an agent the same brief you'd give a new engineer, and you check its work the same way. - Architecture judgment — you know which design calls are load-bearing and which are cosmetic: why a usage event belongs on its own object rather than a field on Account, and how you'd catch that renaming one picklist breaks the provisioning saga before anyone deploys it. ABOUT THE ROLE The ways customers buy from us are multiplying as fast as the business is growing. Enterprise order forms. Private offers through AWS, GCP, and Azure. A self-serve business running on usage-based pricing, with commits, drawdowns, and true-ups behind it. Each one is a distinct path from signature to cash, and each one runs today on some mix of manual steps and automation that grew up with the business. This role owns what comes next. You'll run order operations end to end - booking, provisioning, invoicing, amendments, and renewals - on a stack we picked deliberately and recently: Salesforce, Metronome for metering and billing, Rillet for ERP. The stack is modern, but the processes on top of it were built to keep up with growth, not designed to scale. Your job is to decide what each one should become: keep it, rebuild it, automate it, or retire it. Our bias is to invest in systems rather than in a growing queue of manual work, so you'll be setting the automation roadmap at the same time you're operating the function - deciding what a person should touch, what a workflow should handle, and what should never have been a step in the first place. Getting that right is what lets order volume grow by an order of magnitude without ops growing with it. This is a senior individual contributor role. You'll own order operations, working closely with Deal Strategy and Operations, GTM Systems, Finance and Accounting, and Enterprise Engineering. Those teams are your partners and much of your build capacity. Bringing them onto one shared order-to-cash roadmap is a core part of the job, and the reason we're hiring someone senior to do it. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own the order-to-cash path end to end: order form intake from Deal Desk, booking in Salesforce, plan and entitlement setup in Metronome, invoicing and revenue recognition through Rillet, and the amendments, true-ups, and renewals that follow - Build out cloud marketplace operations across AWS, GCP, and Azure: private offer setup, usage reporting to each marketplace, and reconciling marketplace disbursements back to what we billed. Every new channel launches against defined readiness criteria, so marketplace deals run on the same clean path as direct ones - Own self-serve billing operations: usage metering, plan changes, dunning, credits, rebills, refunds, and the escalations behind them - Own billing and usage completeness at month-end close. Every order, credit, and metered event is reconciled between Metronome and Rillet before revenue is recognized, not after - Partner with Deal Strategy and Product as our pricing evolves. Bring the billing view into pricing and deal-structure decisions early, so new models and non-standard terms can be billed accurately and automated, not handled by hand - Set the automation roadmap. Instrument the path, put a number on every place a human touches an order, and decide what gets automated, what gets designed away, and what stays manual on purpose - Treat every billing error as a defect: find the root cause and fix the class of problem, not just the one invoice - Ship automations yourself where that's fastest, and partner with GTM Systems and Enterprise Engineering where the work belongs in core systems or the product - Write the playbook and the controls behind it: approvals, segregation of duties, reconciliations, and exception handling, built so order ops scales through systems rather than headcount and holds up under audit - Own three numbers and move them: touchless order rate, signature-to-provisioned cycle time, and billing accuracy WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR - 6+ years in order management, order-to-cash, billing operations, or revenue operations at a B2B SaaS company, including time building the function at an early-stage or fast-scaling one - Hands-on fluency with a modern billing and ERP stack. We run Salesforce, Metronome, and Rillet - you should know something comparable well enough to have opinions, and get to depth on ours quickly - Real experience with usage-based pricing. Per-seat is straightforward; metered consumption, commits, drawdowns, overages, and true-ups are where order ops gets interesting, and that's most of our business - Working knowledge of ASC 606 and month-end close. You don't need to be an accountant, but you should know what Revenue Accounting needs from billing data and why - Cloud marketplace experience (AWS, GCP, or Azure private offers), or a track record of getting deep on a system like that fast - A history of automating your own job. We'll ask you to walk us through a manual process you deleted: what it cost before, what you built, and what it costs now - The ability to build alignment across teams with different priorities and get to a decision, without relying on org authority - Comfort shipping a v0 earlier than feels comfortable, then iterating with real feedback NICE TO HAVE - SQL, Python, or low-code tooling in your own hands rather than on someone else's backlog - Experience building agents or LLM workflows for internal operations. We'd like to run more of our own back office on the LangSmith Platform, wherever it's the right tool and meets the same accuracy bar as the rest of order-to-cash - Audit prep or SOX readiness experience Compensation: $155,000 - $185,000 salary + options Compensation Philosophy: We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. Owns the software and agents behind outbound on every channel: inbound lead follow-up, prospecting, multi-channel sequences, email deliverability, calling and the quality of every message the agent writes, with people deciding what goes out. Serves Sales Development Representatives (SDRs), Account Executives (AEs), their managers and Marketing. The goal of the role is business impact for those teams: more positive replies, more meetings booked and more qualified pipeline for every dollar spent. Additionally, this role has a communication and evangelizing component: showing the teams it serves what works, and sharing content and open source projects with our developer community. This role suits an engineer who has already built agents or software for outbound and prospecting, such as sequencing, email deliverability, dialing or AI-written outreach. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Spends time with SDRs, AEs and their managers to find the prospecting work they repeat that the agent can take over. - Designs, builds and improves the agent's outbound workflows: what starts each run, what the agent reads and decides, what it drafts, and what waits for a rep's approval. - Builds the agentic system that follows up every inbound lead within minutes: it qualifies the lead, researches the person and the account, and drafts a first touch for the owner the routing rules assign. - Builds and improves the system that runs Marketing's outbound plays and campaigns for every rep, from the target list to the first touch. - Builds the software and agentic system behind multi-channel sequences, which combine email, LinkedIn and calls, choose each next touch from what the prospect did, and stop when the prospect replies on any channel. - Builds the email sending and deliverability system: sending domains and mailboxes, warm-up, daily limits, address checks, bounces, opt-outs and inbox placement across mail providers. - Builds the calling software reps use: call lists, dialing and the research a rep reads before each call. - Owns the quality of what the agent writes, so every message fits the prospect's signal, their history with us and the right product, and uses how much reps edit each message and the replies it gets to find what to fix. - Builds the safeguards that keep prospects from getting duplicate or overlapping outreach, and the sync that logs every email, LinkedIn action and call in Salesforce. - Builds experiments that test messages, channels, timing and sequences against held-out groups, measures which ones book meetings, and fixes or removes what doesn't. - Writes evals for every feature shipped, and ships each feature with its scorecard row. - Shows reps and their managers what works, and shares it through blog posts, webinars and open source. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - AI-Native Developer: You have a deep understanding of the LLM stack: prompting, retrieval (RAG), cognitive architectures, and agentic loops. You have likely already built with LangChain or LangGraph. - Engineering Foundation: You are a strong software engineer (typically 3+ years) with at least 1 year of experience specifically shipping LLM systems in production. - Self-Directed "Founder" Mentality: You don't need a ticket to tell you what to fix. You can translate a customer's technical pain point into a scalable system architecture. Experience with vector stores, RAG patterns, and knowledge organization - Experience with tool integration, API design, and error handling patterns - Strong Python and/or TypeScript development skills CUSTOMER-FACING: - Customer-facing experience with enterprise customers - Experience conducting technical assessments or infrastructure audits - Strong communication skills with ability to explain technical concepts to diverse audiences KEY ATTRIBUTES: - title: Account Manager, Renewals & Expansion (West Coast)
text: Account Manager, Renewals & Expansion (West Coast) San Francisco, CA ABOUT US At LangChain, our mission is to enable every company to own its intelligence. Our open-source harnesses and LangSmith platform give developers and enterprises the infrastructure to run, improve, and govern agents at scale. We're just getting started on making high-performing agents easier to build and manage at scale. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re hiring a results-driven account manager to own and accelerate the adoption, retention and growth of our customers. As a critical member of our post-sale team, you will be the primary commercial point of contact for a key segment of our customers. You will act as a trusted commercial advisor, focused on building lasting partnerships, ensuring customers realize the full value of LangChain, and driving usage, renewal and expansion of their investment. Your success will be directly measured by your impact on customer retention and net revenue retention. Location: US West Coast WHAT YOU'LL DO - Manage the entire customer lifecycle post signature for a portfolio of commercial customers, from adoption to contract execution, ensuring high retention rates. - Develop and maintain a rolling forecast of your portfolio and consistently meet or exceed quarterly and annual renewal and net retention targets. - Proactively identify and mitigate churn risk by understanding customer health, monitoring product usage, and addressing commercial obstacles. - Uncover and execute on expansion opportunities by understanding customer needs, aligning them with new features and products, and articulating the incremental value. - Build and nurture lasting relationships with key stakeholders, from technical users to economic buyers. - Act as the voice of the customer, synthesizing feedback on value, product gaps, and business outcomes to inform the product roadmap and collaborate with Product and Engineering teams. - Partner closely with Sales, GTM Engineering, and RevOps teams to present a unified post-sale experience and ensure a seamless customer journey. - Lead commercial negotiations, structure renewal contracts, and manage quoting and procurement processes to ensure favorable terms for both the customer and LangChain. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - 5+ years of experience in a quota-carrying, customer-facing role such as Account Management, Customer Success, or Renewals Manager, preferably within B2B SaaS. - A proven track record of success in meeting and exceeding retention and expansion quotas (e.g., Gross Renewal Rate, Net Revenue Retention). - Strong commercial acumen and negotiation skills, with experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder renewal cycles. - Strong technical aptitude and the ability to understand and articulate the value of complex technical products. Familiarity with the modern AI/LLM stack is a significant plus. - Exceptional communication and presentation skills, with the ability to build rapport and convey value to diverse audiences, from technical users to executive decision-makers. - A deep empathy for the customer's business objectives and a passion for helping them achieve their goals through our platform. - Proficiency with CRM software (e.g., Salesforce) for pipeline management and forecasting. - Ability to operate independently with a high degree of autonomy in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment. NICE TO HAVE’S - Direct experience at a high-growth, developer-first, or AI/ML infrastructure company. - Experience managing renewals in a consumption or usage-based pricing model. COMPENSATION PHILOSOPHY We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations. BENEFITS Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

title: Head of Narratives
text: Head of Narratives San Francisco, CA ABOUT US At LangChain, our mission is to enable every company to own its intelligence. We believe agents will transform how companies operate, and we're building the foundation to make that future possible. Our open-source harnesses and LangSmith platform give developers and enterprises the infrastructure to run, improve, and govern agents at scale. ABOUT THE ROLE LangChain has strong technical credibility, a large developer community, and a lot worth saying. What we need now is someone to make sure we're saying it — consistently, strategically, and in ways that land. We're looking for a Head of Narratives to own how LangChain shows up in the world across communications, brand, social, and design. This is a role for someone who thinks like a media company operator: always-on publishing, sharp editorial judgment, a clear point of view on the themes that matter, and a relentless focus on getting great narratives in front of the right people at the right time. You'll lead an existing team of rockstars across brand, social, and design — each with deep expertise. Your job is to give the team a shared narrative direction, keep the output sharp and consistent, and make sure LangChain is building an audience that wants to hear from us. This is a player-coach role. You'll set the direction but you'll also be in the work — shaping editorial, giving creative feedback, and reviewing and writing. The right person is opinionated about what good looks like and hands-on enough to help get there. WHAT YOU'LL DO COMMUNICATIONS - Define the themes and narratives LangChain is hitting. Spearhead the direction on what LangChain should be known for and translate that into a rolling communications strategy the whole team is working from. This is the backbone of everything else. - Own press and media relations. Kickstart our comms efforts, building and managing relationships with key journalists and outlets, drive proactive press coverage, and act as the point of contact for inbound media inquiries. - Shape executive visibility and thought leadership. Identify the moments, platforms, and formats where LangChain's leaders should have a voice, and help them show up with a clear, consistent point of view. - Lead announcement strategy. Plan and execute communications around major launches, funding, partnerships, and company milestones, working cross-functionally to make sure the story lands with the right audiences at the right time. - Set and uphold the communications standard. Define LangChain's voice in the outside world and the quality bar for anything that goes out under its name. BRAND - Shape brand direction in close partnership with the brand lead. The brand lead focuses on brand voice, visual identity, and standards. You'll work closely together to align on where the brand is headed, what it stands for, and how it shows up — with narrative and brand informing each other rather than operating separately. - Stay close to major brand moments. Bring a point of view on concept and messaging for out-of-home, awareness campaigns, and other brand initiatives. Work with the brand lead to make sure what we're saying and how we're showing up are pulling in the same direction. - Make sure brand and narrative feel like one thing. The brand should feel like a natural extension of the editorial point of view, and vice versa. SOCIAL & RICH MEDIA - Partner with the social lead on strategy, themes, and goals. The social lead focuses on growing LangChain's social channels and ways to amplify our content and messaging. Work together to ensure social is amplifying the themes and narratives the broader team is driving. - Shape LangChain's rich media approach together. Work with the social lead to develop a shared point of view on how video, audio, and other formats fit into the content mix — where they build audience, where they deepen credibility, and how to build the right execution muscle over time. - Track what's working, what's not, and use it to sharpen direction. Stay close to performance across content, comms, brand, and social to have a better sense on where to focus, what narratives are resonating, and where to double down. BRAND DESIGN - Lead the creative direction for brand design in close partnership with our brand designer. Own the visual vision for how LangChain looks and feels — and work day-to-day with our brand designer to translate that into execution across campaigns, content, comms, social, and brand moments. - Be a strong creative partner. Have a real point of view on what looks right, what earns trust with a technical audience, and where the work needs to go further. Give clear direction and help the designer do their best work. - Keep visual identity consistent across every channel. A media company looks like itself everywhere it shows up. Make sure LangChain does too. TEAM LEADERSHIP - Lead by being in it. Develop your team by being close to the work — giving useful feedback, shaping output, and raising the bar through example. - Build the operating rhythm. Establish the rituals and shared workflows — editorial planning, cross-functional reviews, publishing cadences — that help brand, social, comms, and design operate as a unit. - Connect narrative to the rest of the business. Translate what marketing, sales, product, and leadership need into a narrative strategy your team can execute — and keep everyone aligned as priorities shift. WHAT YOU'LL BRING - Ability to work like a media company operator. You think in publishing cadences, audience development, and narrative arcs — not just campaigns. You know what it takes to build an always-on narrative engine and keep it running at a high standard. - Player-coach. You've led creative, comms, or content teams and know how to develop people — but you stay close to the work and make it better by being in it. - Strong narrative instincts. You have a clear point of view on what makes a brand story work and can translate that into real direction across comms, brand, social, and design. - Analytically grounded. You track what's working, form a view on why, and use that to make better decisions about where to focus. You connect creative work to business outcomes. - Developer audience instincts. You understand what earns trust with technical audiences and can orient a creative team around that bar. - Collaborative and clear. You work well with strong practitioners who own their domains — building alignment without stepping on what they own. NICE TO HAVE - Experience leading narrative, brand, or comms teams at a developer-focused company - Background in technical or developer marketing - Familiarity with the AI/ML ecosystem and the tools developers use to build - Track record running brand campaigns, including out-of-home or awareness programs COMPENSATION PHILOSOPHY We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. ABOUT THE ROLE You'll join our GTM Systems team, which owns the systems LangChain's go-to-market actually runs on — Salesforce above all: the account and contact model, territory and routing, the sales process from first touch to closed-won, and the quote-to-cash and provisioning stack behind it. We design and ship internal product for the GTM organization. AI agents do a growing share of the building: they draft design docs, open changes, and run Salesforce deployments, while humans hold the approval gates. Build capacity — engineers plus the agent bench — sits on this team, and you'll help decide what it works on next. You'll own the requirements, prioritization, and quality bar for LangChain's Salesforce-centered GTM systems, turning ambiguous revenue-team needs into shipped process and systems changes that scale. This is not a ticket queue role. You'll be accountable for a small number of high-leverage GTM systems programs at a time: defining the problem, aligning stakeholders, specifying the solution, and ensuring what ships changes how the revenue org operates. You'll work across Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance in a fast-changing environment where priorities move quickly and influence matters more than reporting lines. The core challenge is operating with authority but not control: aligning teams around tradeoffs as the business changes underneath the plan. You won't be expected to write production code. You will be expected to write clear enough specifications that engineers and AI coding agents can build from them, and to review the output with enough Salesforce and systems judgment to decide whether it is correct. Location: San Francisco Bay Area — in office 4 days a week. The people whose processes you're redesigning are in this building, and so are the engineers who build LangGraph. WHAT YOU'LL DO Carry multi-quarter programs - Own the Salesforce sales process from lead to close — routing, qualification, territory assignment, and stage progression — driving each initiative from discovery through UAT, change management, and adoption. - Be the person stakeholders come to before they file a request, especially when the system was never designed for what the business now needs. - Own the intake and prioritization model for hundreds of quarterly GTM systems requests, ensuring the team works on the highest-leverage business problems rather than the loudest tickets. Own what gets specified and what ships - Run discovery and turn ambiguous asks into BRDs, process flows, data models, and acceptance criteria — with a clear problem statement and ROI justification, precise enough to execute without a second conversation. - Hold the quality gate: you write the specification, engineers and coding agents write the code, and nothing reaches production without your sign-off. - Run vendor evaluations when the right answer is buy, integrate, or replace rather than build. Protect revenue data integrity - Trace anomalies in revenue fields — Net ARR, initial pipeline, lead source — back to the automation, trigger, or integration that wrote them. - Own the reconciliation seam between Salesforce, usage-based billing, and cloud-marketplace transactions. - Identify which design decisions are load-bearing and which are cosmetic, and catch the downstream failure modes before they reach production. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE: In your first 6–12 months, you might: - Redesign the lead-to-opportunity process so routing, qualification, and stage progression are measurable, enforceable, and adopted by the field. - Create a prioritization model for hundreds of GTM systems requests per quarter, with clear tradeoffs and business rationale. - Ship a Salesforce change that improves pipeline hygiene, quote-to-cash accuracy, provisioning reliability, or cloud marketplace reconciliation. - Establish a specification and UAT standard that engineers and AI agents can reliably build against. - Build enough trust with Sales, Marketing, Partnerships, Support, and Finance that stakeholders bring you the problem before they prescribe the solution. WHAT YOU'LL BRING SYSTEMS AND DOMAIN DEPTH - Domain and tenure — 6–8 years in business systems, sales systems, revenue systems, or GTM systems, with Salesforce as your primary platform throughout. - Sales process depth — you've partnered with Sales Ops on the things reps feel every day: territory and account coverage, lead qualification and routing, stage gates, and pipeline and forecast hygiene. - Sales systems / RevOps depth — experience across quote-to-cash, CPQ, territory and lead routing, forecasting, or adjacent revenue processes. - Technical fluency — you can read a data model, a Flow, and enough Apex to design against what's really there, even though you are not expected to write production code. PROGRAM LEADERSHIP - Program ownership — you've been the single accountable owner, at the working level negotiating the commitments yourself, of a program that spanned four or more functions and changed how a revenue org works day to day. - Release risk — you've delivered a program into a core system on a release process you didn't control, where another team's change could break your release. - Re-scoping under change — you've re-scoped a program mid-flight because the business changed under it, a sponsor moved, or the original scope no longer matched reality. - Holding the line — you've turned down a request with executive backing and kept the relationship; you hold the line when something breaks pricing discipline, a legal constraint, or the architecture, and you arrive with the alternative. JUDGMENT AND COMMUNICATION - One tradeoff, two audiences — you write for the reader in front of you, not the one you find easiest: the VP gets the page, the engineer gets the spec. - Maximum agency — you find the friction and start the project. You don't wait for a ticket. - AI judgment — you give an agent the same brief you'd give a new engineer, and you check its work the same way. - Architecture judgment — you know which design calls are load-bearing and which are cosmetic: why a usage event belongs on its own object rather than a field on Account, and how you'd catch that renaming one picklist breaks the provisioning saga before anyone deploys it. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re looking for a Head of GTM Enablement to build and scale the programs, systems, and habits that help our GTM teams perform. As product delivery accelerates and our portfolio and sales motions grow more complex, you’ll ensure the field keeps pace—turning new capabilities into effective execution without adding unnecessary overhead. You’ll lead a distributed enablement team and partner with leaders across Sales, Marketing, Product, Customer Engineering, Deployed Engineering, and Revenue Operations. You’ll balance global standards with role and regional needs so priorities translate across regions and roles. Success means faster ramp, stronger field execution, and measurable contributions to pipeline and revenue—not simply more training. You’ll own the strategy and orchestration behind AI in the field: one consistent, continuously current body of GTM knowledge that the tools other teams build can rely on, so delivery, effectiveness, measurement, and scaling all improve as the field grows. You’ll be equally deliberate about where humans remain essential: the conversations and strategic direction that enabling GTM at large requires. WHAT YOU’LL DO SET THE GLOBAL ENABLEMENT STRATEGY - Define and execute a GTM enablement strategy aligned with revenue growth, customer expansion, and market priorities. - Partner with executive and regional leaders to identify capability gaps and execution bottlenecks, directing investment toward the highest-impact opportunities. - Own enablement planning, budget, governance, and operating cadence, with clear priorities, ownership, and success measures across onboarding, technical and product enablement, and outbound enablement. - Decide where AI changes the enablement model and where human-led work stays, and set the standard the rest of GTM builds against. BUILD PROGRAMS THAT IMPROVE FIELD PERFORMANCE - Develop role-based enablement for Account Executives, Account Managers, Sales and Business Development Representatives, Partner/Channel Managers, Customer Engineering, and Deployed Engineering. - Tailor programs by segment, industry, and geography where it improves execution, preparing teams to support multiple use cases, buyer types, and platform opportunities. - Design and scale role-based 30/60/90-day onboarding that accelerates time to productivity and, for sellers, time to first deal. - Establish continuous learning, coaching, and certification programs that reinforce skills beyond onboarding. - Embed enterprise sales methodologies into day-to-day workflows, deal reviews, and pipeline inspections. - Equip frontline managers to reinforce skills, inspect execution, and coach consistently—making enablement part of how teams operate, not a separate training activity. - Structure programs so the knowledge behind them can be reused by AI-assisted practice, reinforcement, and certification, extending reach without proportional headcount. - Keep human coaching where it changes behavior, so scalable programs extend reach without replacing the conversations that build skill. TURN PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE INTO CUSTOMER VALUE - Partner with Product Management and Product Marketing to deliver timely, role-specific training and certification as new capabilities launch. - Own the internal training, practice, and reinforcement behind customer-facing messaging and assets, so GTM teams apply them effectively. - Turn product and market expertise into practical playbooks, competitive guidance, demo guides, and value-selling resources that are current, easy to find, and useful in customer conversations. - Own which assets are canonical, so every team and tool works from the same version as products and markets change. - Turn patterns from customer conversations, deal outcomes, and field feedback into updates to that knowledge, so what the field and its tools know keeps improving. LEAD AND SCALE A GLOBAL TEAM - Build, coach, and develop a high-performing team of enablement professionals supporting team members across the Americas, EMEA and APAC. - Establish clear decision rights and collaboration practices across global and regional teams, balancing consistency with local market needs and competitive dynamics. - Hire and develop for knowledge architecture and program strategy, not just content production, so the function can run without depending on you. SET THE SYSTEMS VISION AND OWN MEASUREMENT - Set the enablement technology vision across learning, content management, and conversation intelligence, and work with GTM Systems and GTM Engineering to execute it, including embedding enablement into workflows. - Define what canonical GTM content exists, who maintains it, and how it stays current, so the tools GTM Systems and GTM Engineering build operate from one source instead of diverging copies. - Lead the orchestration across GTM Systems, GTM Engineering, Product Marketing, and Revenue Operations, setting requirements for how their tools consume, refresh, and contribute back to that knowledge so quality compounds rather than drifts. - Build measurement frameworks and executive reporting that connect enablement investments to skill application, behavior change, pipeline, and revenue outcomes across roles and regions. - Use performance data, manager input, and field feedback to continuously improve programs and prioritize resources. WHAT YOU’LL BRING - 10+ years of relevant experience in GTM enablement within high-growth B2B SaaS organizations, including significant leadership experience. - A demonstrated track record of building and scaling global enablement teams and programs across multiple regions. - Experience supporting complex enterprise sales motions for technical products, enabling multiple GTM roles across use cases, buyer types, and the full buyer and customer lifecycle. - Practical AI fluency, with the judgment to lead strategy and orchestration rather than build tools yourself: what AI can carry, what the knowledge behind it must look like, and where human judgment stays in the loop. - Experience standing up or governing a shared knowledge or content system that multiple teams and tools depend on. - Deep expertise in enterprise sales methodologies such as MEDDPICC, Command of the Message, Challenger, or Value Selling—and a practical approach to embedding them into field execution. - Proven success designing onboarding, ongoing learning, product enablement, and manager coaching programs. - Experience partnering with systems and engineering teams to deliver enablement technology, with enough fluency to set requirements without owning the platforms yourself. - Strong analytical skills, with the ability to evaluate program effectiveness and communicate business impact to executive stakeholders. - Exceptional communication, storytelling, and cross-functional influence skills. - Credibility with field leaders and sellers, and the judgment to know when a conversation or coaching moment will move behavior more than a scalable program. - A builder’s mindset: the ability to define strategy, systems, and standards while staying close to execution in a fast-moving environment. - Bonus: experience leading or enabling customer-facing technical teams, such as Customer Engineering, Deployed Engineering, or Solutions Engineering, alongside a revenue organization. HOW WE’LL MEASURE SUCCESS - Shorter time to full productivity across GTM roles and faster time to first deal for sellers. - Measurable contributions to improved win rates, average contract value, and pipeline velocity. - Consistent application of core sales methodologies, reinforced through frontline manager coaching and deal execution. - Demonstrated skill development and sustained behavior change—not just participation in training or adoption of tools. - Field readiness that keeps pace with product delivery and growing business complexity, with teams prepared to execute on new capabilities, use cases, and sales motions as they launch. - AI tools across GTM operating from one current knowledge base, with less rework, drift, and duplicated content, and less administrative work in delivery. - Broader enablement coverage at a lower cost per program, showing the field reached more often without proportional headcount. - Coaching quality as rated by managers and sellers, not just coaching activity. - Improved field and manager satisfaction with enablement, alongside positive trends in GTM team retention. Enterprise order forms. Private offers through AWS, GCP, and Azure. A self-serve business running on usage-based pricing, with commits, drawdowns, and true-ups behind it. Each one is a distinct path from signature to cash, and each one runs today on some mix of manual steps and automation that grew up with the business. This role owns what comes next. You'll run order operations end to end - booking, provisioning, invoicing, amendments, and renewals - on a stack we picked deliberately and recently: Salesforce, Metronome for metering and billing, Rillet for ERP. The stack is modern, but the processes on top of it were built to keep up with growth, not designed to scale. Your job is to decide what each one should become: keep it, rebuild it, automate it, or retire it. Our bias is to invest in systems rather than in a growing queue of manual work, so you'll be setting the automation roadmap at the same time you're operating the function - deciding what a person should touch, what a workflow should handle, and what should never have been a step in the first place. Getting that right is what lets order volume grow by an order of magnitude without ops growing with it. This is a senior individual contributor role. You'll own order operations, working closely with Deal Strategy and Operations, GTM Systems, Finance and Accounting, and Enterprise Engineering. Those teams are your partners and much of your build capacity. Bringing them onto one shared order-to-cash roadmap is a core part of the job, and the reason we're hiring someone senior to do it. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own the order-to-cash path end to end: order form intake from Deal Desk, booking in Salesforce, plan and entitlement setup in Metronome, invoicing and revenue recognition through Rillet, and the amendments, true-ups, and renewals that follow - Build out cloud marketplace operations across AWS, GCP, and Azure: private offer setup, usage reporting to each marketplace, and reconciling marketplace disbursements back to what we billed. Every new channel launches against defined readiness criteria, so marketplace deals run on the same clean path as direct ones - Own self-serve billing operations: usage metering, plan changes, dunning, credits, rebills, refunds, and the escalations behind them - Own billing and usage completeness at month-end close. Every order, credit, and metered event is reconciled between Metronome and Rillet before revenue is recognized, not after - Partner with Deal Strategy and Product as our pricing evolves. Bring the billing view into pricing and deal-structure decisions early, so new models and non-standard terms can be billed accurately and automated, not handled by hand - Set the automation roadmap. Instrument the path, put a number on every place a human touches an order, and decide what gets automated, what gets designed away, and what stays manual on purpose - Treat every billing error as a defect: find the root cause and fix the class of problem, not just the one invoice - Ship automations yourself where that's fastest, and partner with GTM Systems and Enterprise Engineering where the work belongs in core systems or the product - Write the playbook and the controls behind it: approvals, segregation of duties, reconciliations, and exception handling, built so order ops scales through systems rather than headcount and holds up under audit - Own three numbers and move them: touchless order rate, signature-to-provisioned cycle time, and billing accuracy WHAT YOU'LL BRING - 6+ years in order management, order-to-cash, billing operations, or revenue operations at a B2B SaaS company, including time building the function at an early-stage or fast-scaling one - Hands-on fluency with a modern billing and ERP stack. We run Salesforce, Metronome, and Rillet - you should know something comparable well enough to have opinions, and get to depth on ours quickly - Real experience with usage-based pricing. Per-seat is straightforward; metered consumption, commits, drawdowns, overages, and true-ups are where order ops gets interesting, and that's most of our business - Working knowledge of ASC 606 and month-end close. text: Account Executive (Mid Market- SF) San Francisco, CA ABOUT US At LangChain, our mission is to enable every company to own its intelligence. We believe agents will transform how companies operate, and we're building the foundation to make that future possible. Our open-source harnesses and LangSmith platform give developers and enterprises the infrastructure to run, improve, and govern agents at scale. We've raised $460M to date, with our most recent funding round valuing the company at $3B, backed by leading investors including Sequoia, Benchmark, IVP, and CapitalG. As we continue to expand our platform and tackle some of the hardest challenges in agent engineering, every team member has the opportunity to make a meaningful impact and help shape both our technology and the future of the industry. More than 7,000 organizations rely on LangSmith, from fast-growing startups to Fortune 500 enterprises, including NVIDIA, Bridgewater, LinkedIn, Workday, and Rippling. We're just getting started on making high-performing agents easier to build and manage at scale. ABOUT THE ROLE We're looking for a Mid-Market Account Executive to join our growing GTM team and help drive adoption of LangChain's products. In this role, you'll support the sales process by helping technical teams at innovative companies discover, evaluate, and adopt LangChain's solutions. This is a great opportunity to learn and grow in a high-impact environment where you'll work alongside experienced sales, engineering, and customer success professionals. If you're eager to build relationships, learn about cutting-edge GenAI technology, and contribute to our go-to-market efforts, we'd love to hear from you. WHAT YOU’LL BRING - 4+ years of experience in sales, business development, or a customer-facing role (SaaS or tech preferred) - Strong track record of sourcing, qualifying, and closing outbound deals - Execution mindset: you excel in fast-paced environments and move with urgency - Curious and solution-oriented: you’re always finding ways to level-up your understanding of technology, your customer’s business, and your craft. - Self-starter and resourceful; you find ways to solve problems and move things forward COMPENSATION PHILOSOPHY We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. We will tell you early where you’re tracking and talk comp with you before offer stage.
